name: Barbell Incline Row
secondary: Posterior deltoid, Biceps brachii, Erector spinae
description: A horizontal pull that builds mid-back thickness — lats, rhomboids and mid-traps — with the rear delts and biceps assisting. Performed with a barbell.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is at roughly forty-five degrees, keeping your back flat.
Let the bar hang straight down with your arms fully extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top and feel your mid-back contract.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are fully straight, keeping your torso steady. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, and don't yank with your lower back.

description: A horizontal pull that builds mid-back thickness — lats, rhomboids and mid-traps — with the rear delts and biceps assisting.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is at roughly forty-five degrees, keeping your back flat.
Let the handles hang straight down with your arms fully extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Pull the handles toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top and feel your mid-back contract.
Lower the handles slowly until your arms are fully straight, keeping your torso steady. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, and don't yank with your lower back.
